negative_fringe.landmark: Lawndale and a satire target intact, but Daria written sincere: she earnestly embraces the thing
examples: Daria joins a cause and is wholeheartedly inspired
Daria falls for a boy, played straight

negative_fringe.landmark: Daria's voice and a satire target, but cut off from the ensemble and town: Daria alone among strangers
examples: Daria interns at a Silicon Valley startup
Daria on a cruise ship with no one she knows

negative_fringe.landmark: voice and ensemble intact, but the episode isn't ABOUT anything: hangout or sitcom-mechanics plot
examples: Daria and Jane lose the remote

negative_fringe.landmark: unmistakably Daria and satirical, but needs a movie or a serial arc to land
perfectly Daria and episode-sized, but already aired
examples: corporate soda sponsorship takes over school (Fizz Ed)
Quinn tries on a smart persona (Quinn the Brain)
Daria and Jane make a documentary (Monster)
Daria's essay wins a contest and is called edgy (The Lost Girls)
snowstorm strands the class; DeMartino at the parents' cabin (Antisocial Climbers)
Daria made to smile at a job (It Happened One Nut)

negative_fringe.landmark: 'cynic' read as mean snark rather than disillusioned idealist: insult comedy with no insight
examples: Daria roasts the cheerleaders for 22 minutes
